frames.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Produce ONE full-frame cinematic photoreal impact animation in-between, not a montage or a blended double exposure. Image 1 is the pristine frozen master/edit target; Image 2 is the early flash endpoint; Image 3 is the later developed plume endpoint. All three show the SAME locked camera and planet. Preserve the master's exact dimensions, framing, horizon, sun, stars, oceans, clouds, geography, islands and grading. Modify ONLY the local impact region, centered at 62% across and 63% down. Impact stays rooted at this identical surface point. Keep image edges and distant scenery identical. The event should naturally evolve from image 2 toward image 3; retain the same overall plume family, lighting and perspective. No intact asteroid, no laser, no text/UI, no new background objects. Requested frame: about 12 seconds after impact, FIRST of FOUR intermediate stages. A compact brilliant orange-white vapor dome has begun to expand and cool from the flash. A low turbulent bronze-gray ejecta curtain and a thin white ocean-steam skirt surround the base. Very little vertical rise: top around y=55%, base around y=66%, total width about 15% of frame. This is much smaller and lower than image 3, still mostly luminous vapor near the ocean. Preserve fine film-VFX detail and the immense planetary scale. This must be a new physically legible stage of growth, not a semitransparent copy of the final plume.
